attributes.probed_form: Baseline (retained), src/game/movie/movieplayer.cpp:2077: `q = param_2 + (u32)ofs + 0xC;`.  AXIS 1, drop the cast so the two pointer/int terms associate first: `q = param_2 + ofs + 0xC;` -> REGRESSED real 76 -> 91 and, decisively, O203 against T204: without the cast MWCC CSEs `param_2 + ofs` against the neighbouring `ReadF32LE(param_2 + ofs + 4)` at line 2074 and one `add` disappears.  AXIS 2, keep the cast and force the association by splitting the statement: `q = param_2 + (u32)ofs;` then `q += 0xC;` -> REGRESSED real 87, still O203, and far worse structurally: MWCC absorbed the +0xC into thirteen downstream field displacements (ours `addi r3,r30,16/20/24/...` against target `addi r3,r29,4/8/12/...`), taking regnorm from 0 STRUCTURAL to 19.
attributes.residual: NAMED MECHANISM, two words, do-not-retry on cast removal and on statement splitting. regnorm: 255 paired, 37 renaming, 0 STRUCTURAL, 2 unpaired. The two words are the SAME address computation spelled in the opposite order -- target `add r29,r28,r26` then `addi r29,r29,12` (the two variables sum first, the constant last), ours `addi r30,r28,12` then `add r30,r26,r30` (the constant binds to the offset first). r26 is param_2, r28 is the running `ofs` accumulator. They are reported UNPAIRED rather than STRUCTURAL only because the pair sits one instruction apart. The cast in `param_2 + (u32)ofs + 0xC` is doing real work and must stay: it is the only thing preventing MWCC from CSEing this base against the textually adjacent `param_2 + ofs + 4` at line 2074, and that CSE costs instruction-count parity, so any future axis must keep the cast and move only the association. Worth noting for whoever resumes: the SAME source file computes the sibling base at line 2074 with the constant binding FIRST and the target agrees with us there, so the two sites genuinely differ in the original source and must not be unified.
